title: Floor 1: The double shift
task: Return exactly one row per trip key, and every column of trips_raw. A trip key is the set of columns that together identify one trip. Two trips that differ in any amount are different trips. row_id and loaded_at describe the load, not the trip.

guideTask: Return exactly one row per trip key, and every column of trips_raw. A trip key is the set of columns that together identify one trip. Two trips that differ in any amount are different trips. row_id and loaded_at describe the load, not the trip.
context: The depot dashboard is overstating revenue because one delivery arrived twice. trips_raw holds every physical row in the incoming feed, including both copies, and zones names the locations. Keep one whole row per trip so the morning report counts each ride once.

refresher.title: A query in steps: WITH
refresher.text: WITH names a query result so the next step can read it. The final SELECT returns your answer. These steps are one query; you do not need to save a table.
refresher.sql:
WITH rides(id) AS (VALUES (1), (2))
SELECT count(*) AS rides FROM rides;

refresher.title: A key, grain and repeated groups
refresher.text: Grain means what one row represents. A key is the set of columns that identifies one item at that grain. GROUP BY collects rows with the same key; HAVING filters the groups after counting. DISTINCT compares only the columns you select.

refresher.title: Keep a whole row from each group
refresher.text: ROW_NUMBER numbers rows inside each PARTITION BY group. ORDER BY chooses which copy comes first. Put the numbered rows in a CTE, then use WHERE rn = 1 in the final SELECT to keep one whole row per group. Leave rn out of the answer.

rulesText:
## Floor 1: The double shift (duplicates)

- **Tables given:** `trips_raw`, `zones`.
- **The dirt (planted):** the load for pickups on 2024-01-15 ran twice. The 174 second copies have
  new `row_id` values and `loaded_at = 2024-02-01 06:40`. So `SELECT DISTINCT *` removes nothing.
- **Trip key:** `(vendor_id, pickup_at, dropoff_at, pu_location_id, do_location_id, total_amount)`.
  In the full January file this key has no duplicates (checked: 0 duplicate groups in 2,964,624 rows).
- **Task:** return an answer with exactly one row per trip key, every column of `trips_raw`.
- **Expected:** 7,345 rows in, 7,171 out. Revenue (`sum(total_amount)`) 197,977.97 in, 193,403.10 out.
- **Pass:** the answer has the columns of `trips_raw` (any order, extra columns not allowed);
  every row in it is an unchanged row of `trips_raw` (multiset check on all columns);
  7,171 rows; 7,171 distinct trip keys. Which copy survives does not matter.
- **Aha line:** a duplicate is defined by a key you choose, not by "every column equal". Count before, count after, and explain the difference (174 = the rerun).

aboutData.description: These are NYC Taxi and Limousine Commission yellow taxi trip records for January 2024, with a location lookup and the game's teaching changes.
aboutData.loadMetadata: row_id and loaded_at describe the load, not the trip.
aboutData.locations: Location 264 means Unknown (zone N/A); 265 means Outside of NYC.
aboutData.renames: The game renames columns, for example tpep_pickup_datetime becomes pickup_at, and adds row_id and loaded_at. Use the game's column list above when writing your SQL.

taskContext: The depot needs one reliable record per trip before it can report rides and revenue.

The checklist shows whether Answer has been run and its last row count. SQL refresher and About the data links beside it open the guide in a new tab.

Use the task panel checklist after each Run answer: an empty Answer result shows zero rows. Scratch table changes never count as an Answer run. Check floor grades your current Answer query; a row count alone does not mean correct. The panel remembers your collapse choice in the page address.

The task panel checklist starts at Answer: not run yet, then reports Answer: N rows (last run). It preserves that last-run count while you edit Answer or use Scratch. Compare it with the full rules; Check floor evaluates the current query independently of the last run.

Under Tables above Scratch, open a table chip to see its columns and types. Start with trips_raw to find the available names before writing a query. Opening a chip leaves your SQL and Result alone; Enter or Space opens and closes it from the keyboard.

The columns and types describe the table on the active floor, including tables you create. When you replace a table, an open chip refreshes its column view. After switching floors, open the new floor’s chip to inspect that floor’s columns and types.

Use the table chip’s columns and types to choose names for SELECT, WHERE and joins. The column view reads the table quietly: it adds no query to your history or the tutor’s recent queries and never replaces unfinished SQL.

Choose Preview beside any table chip under Tables to see its first 10 rows in a separate panel beside the console, or below it on a narrow screen. Start with trips_raw to see what a row holds. Preview leaves Scratch, Result and query records alone; Close preview takes you back to the chip.

Preview shows up to 10 rows from the table on this floor, including your own outputs. An empty table still shows its column names. Preview refreshes after a replacement and closes when you drop its table or change floors. The panel scrolls sideways for wide rows on a phone.

Preview is a quiet SELECT * with LIMIT 10, without a guaranteed sort order. It does not add a run to either query record. When a transaction is open, Preview explains that you must COMMIT or ROLLBACK before reading rows; it shows columns without running row expressions or changing your transaction.

Use Scratch to explore the given tables or make your own tables. Put one SELECT or WITH query in Answer. Run answer shows its rows in Result; Check floor grades only that query against the original given tables. You do not need to save a table.

Answer uses only this floor’s original given tables, even if you change or drop a table in Scratch. Check floor leaves both boxes, Scratch and Result alone. The task checklist says Answer: not run yet, then shows the row count from your last Run answer; it does not say the answer is correct.

Run answer and Check floor accept the same single SELECT or WITH query. Use Scratch for other statements. Answer text is saved separately for each floor and survives reload, floor switches and Restart floor. Run answer adds an answer entry to both query records; Check floor adds no run.
